meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'introduce'.

examples.text: Мы не будем вводить это блюдо в меню.
examples.trans: We will not introduce this dish into the menu.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и вводить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and introduce on time.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'verdict', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: The judge delivered a strict verdict.

examples.text: Молчи и слушай строгий вердикт жюри.
examples.trans: Keep quiet and listen to the jury's strict verdict.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'hypnosis' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: В отеле возможно появление мошенника и гипнотизёра.
examples.trans: The appearance of a fraudster and hypnotist in the hotel is possible.
The hypnotist is still in the hotel!

meanings.note: Singular only. Common neuter noun meaning 'childhood' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: В детстве я жил в Москве.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other, another, different').

meanings.note: думать о + prepositional = to think about

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: In the sky. Common feminine noun meaning 'star; celebrity' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'star; celebrity' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are bright stars in the sky.

examples.text: Вот молодёжь, ничего не знают! Это же Лещенко! Звезда!
examples.trans: Young people these days, they don't know anything! That's Leshchenko! A star!

meanings.note: declines like какой: какая-то, какое-то, какие-то

examples.trans: What nonsense. But on the other hand, what have I got to lose?

meanings.note: Чн is pronounced шн. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: colloquial: Это кошмар! = That's awful / a nightmare!

examples.trans: That's a nightmare, I don't argue.

examples.text: Это кошмар, я не спорю. Но зачем на видео снимать?
examples.trans: That's a nightmare, I don't argue. But why film it on video?

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.
goes right before the word it negates
Lit. not bad. Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'плохой'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('not bad, decent, fairly good').

examples.text: Это на самом деле неплохой вариант.
examples.trans: This is actually not a bad option.

examples.text: У него неплохой голос для пения.
examples.trans: He has a fairly good singing voice.
They say they cook pretty good dishes there.

meanings.note: usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

That is it, she got really offended.

meanings.note: Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'of the hotel' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Андрей, положи её к себе, а то и эту потеряю.
examples.trans: Andrey, put it in your pocket, or I will lose this one too.

examples.text: Я хотел бы просмотреть все документы по закупке продуктов.
examples.trans: I would like to review all the documents on food purchases.

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'staff, personnel' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Then go faster to the staff locker room.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'даваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'respond to / yield to'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и поддаваться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and respond to on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют поддаваться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to respond to.

meanings.en: to please, to be to someone's liking
meanings.note: + dative: тебе понравится = you'll like it

examples.trans: Well, you'll have to! Don't be afraid, you'll like it.

meanings.note: Всё понятно = all clear. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нятно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'repair shop', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Я лично отвёз её в надёжный сервис.
examples.trans: I personally took it to a reliable repair service.

examples.text: Я просто переживаю за вечерний сервис.
examples.trans: I am simply worried about the evening service.

стараться.gloss: to try, to make an effort

meanings.en: to try hard, to make an effort
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тараться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to try, to make an effort', paired with 'постараться'.

examples.trans: He always tries to help his friends.

examples.text: Марина, зря вы стараетесь. Он никогда не уйдёт от своей Аллы Евгеньевны.
examples.trans: Marina, you're trying in vain. He will never leave his Alla Evgenyevna.

meanings.note: с другой стороны = on the other hand
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'торона'). Common feminine noun meaning 'side' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: On the other hand, it's interesting.
The shop is on that side.

examples.text: Бред какой-то. Но, с другой стороны, чем я рискую?
examples.trans: What nonsense. But on the other hand, what have I got to lose?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'trance' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Wait, this is from the central office.

examples.text: Конечно, выживет! Там травмы не такие тяжёлые.

examples.text: Что-то он долго. Она его в транс вводит!

meanings.note: + genitive singular: три дня. Core Russian num meaning 'three' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: The entire entity; in whole. Common neuter noun meaning 'whole' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ну, в целом эта еда нормальная.
